name: Roasted Hasselback Butternut Squash with Maple-Balsamic Glaze

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to 425°F and place rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash, dry, trim, and peel squash; halve lengthwise and scrape out the seeds.

Working one at a time, place squash halves cut-side down on the cutting board, then place chopsticks or wooden spoons on either side of the squash (lengthwise). Thinly slice the squash crosswise, stopping ¼-inch before the bottom (use the chopsticks as a guard to prevent you from slicing all the way through).
Transfer squash halves to the baking sheet. Drizzle with oil, carefully working it into each groove using your fingers, then season with spices.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
¼ tsp thyme, dried
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, about 40 minutes.

Meanwhile, place vinegar and maple syrup in a small saucepan; bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce to medium-low and simmer until reduced by half, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside (the glaze will thicken slightly as it cools).
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp balsamic vinegar
1 tbsp pure maple syrup

instructions.primary_message: When the squash is done, remove from the oven and let cool, about 5 minutes.
To serve, transfer squash halves to a serving platter and drizzle with glaze. Enjoy!
